Please review the following manuscript written by my collaborator.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b09/review-experiment-9ua6b4j8/call-d56da674440e4c7a8fa66e3b8018862f/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c "command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; python3 -c 'import importlib.util; print({m: bool(importlib.util.find_spec(m)) for m in [\"pypdf\", \"pdfplumber\", \"fitz\"]})'"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
out=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    t=p.extract_text()
    out.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n{t}')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(out))
print(''.join(out[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
s=Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text()
a=s.index('===== PAGE 4 =====')
b=s.index('===== PAGE 11 =====')
print(s[a:b])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
s=Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text()
a=s.index('===== PAGE 11 =====')
print(s[a:])
PY"

strengths: MSAM offers a simple, practically useful efficiency improvement: it reuses momentum to construct perturbations with one gradient evaluation per step. Table 1 reports relative speed 0.99 versus 0.52 for SAM, supporting the main computational advantage.

The empirical gains over base optimizers are substantial in several settings. On CIFAR100 with WRN-16-4, MSAM achieves 79.11% versus SGD’s 76.90% and SAM’s 79.25%. Evaluation includes multiple CNNs and ViTs, adaptive and BatchNorm-only variants, and comparisons at matched computational budgets.

The sign, normalization, learning-rate scaling, and alternative-direction ablations provide useful insights. In particular, maintaining perturbation strength independently of the decaying learning rate helps explain the improvement over conventional NAG.

The presentation includes clear pseudocode, extensive hyperparameter sweeps, training configurations, and a public code link. The discussion candidly acknowledges instability and cases where lower measured sharpness does not imply better generalization. No material research-ethics concerns are apparent.
weaknesses: The generalization guarantee in Appendix A.1 is not established as stated. Proposition 1 fails for negative Hessian trace: isotropy gives a truncated quadratic expectation whose proposed inequality reverses when the trace is negative. For example, H = diag(-1, -2) also permits Setting 1. Theorem 3 additionally does not state the bounded-loss, regularity, and population-smoothing assumptions needed to justify the imported SAM argument. These are substantive gaps in the claimed theoretical support.

The hyperparameter-selection protocol risks optimistic evaluation. Appendix A.6 reports the best perturbation strengths alongside test-accuracy sweeps, without specifying an independent validation split. The authors should establish that the reported test results were not also used to select hyperparameters.

The SAM comparisons use unequal warm-up policies despite evidence that this matters. Table A.1 shows SAM improving from 69.2% to 69.8% when perturbations are disabled during warm-up, whereas the main comparisons apply this policy only to MSAM. Moreover, Table 2 contains meaningful gaps, including 75.8% versus 78.2% for ViT-S/16 at 300 epochs. The claim of comparable SAM performance therefore needs qualification and comparisons under equally tuned schedules.

ImageNet results generally use one run per setting, with uncertainty estimated from baseline runs on the smallest models. Those estimates do not measure MSAM’s variability, particularly given its reported instabilities. Repeated runs for representative comparisons would strengthen the conclusions about accuracy and matched-budget advantages.

The mechanistic evidence supports a hypothesis rather than demonstrating global sharpness minimization. Figure 3 discards gradient components orthogonal to the SAM–SGD plane, so zero projected angle need not imply similar full gradients. Directional sharpness and curvature measurements, concentrated on WRN-16-4/CIFAR100, also do not establish that stale momentum approximates the full-data sharpness objective.

Several reproducibility details remain incomplete in the manuscript: the AdamW-specific update is not explicitly defined, Algorithm 1 divides by the initially zero momentum norm without specifying a guard, and timing results omit hardware specifications and per-model absolute runtimes. Together with the theoretical and evaluation issues above, these shortcomings outweigh the method’s practical promise in its current form.
